data.description:
## Description

**What**: Verify the existing <SUB-AGENT-GUARD> block is preserved verbatim in the new orchestrator SKILL.md after S2's rewrite. Add an automated test that dispatches /dso:onboarding via the Agent tool with a realistic prompt and asserts the literal error string returns. Test must run in CI, not only as an in-session manual check.

**Why**: SC8 mandates the guard is preserved AND the verification mechanism is reproducible across runs. In-session tests vanish after the session ends — they don't catch regressions. The test must live in tests/scripts/ and run via the project's test runner.

**Scope**:
- IN: Verify guard preserved in skills/onboarding/SKILL.md (post-S2). Add a CI-runnable test (extend tests/scripts/test-onboarding-resume.sh with a guard case, OR add tests/scripts/test-onboarding-guard.sh) that dispatches the skill via Agent tool with subagent_type "general-purpose" and asserts the returned text contains the literal string `ERROR: /dso:onboarding requires main session; invoke directly.`
- OUT: Modifications to the guard block content itself (preservation, not redesign). The freshness-predicate tests (S1).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, dispatching /dso:onboarding via the Agent tool with subagent_type "general-purpose" and a prompt that invokes the skill returns the literal text `ERROR: /dso:onboarding requires main session; invoke directly.` (case-sensitive, character-exact)
  ← Satisfies: "The existing <SUB-AGENT-GUARD> blocking sub-agent dispatch INTO /dso:onboarding is preserved."
- When this story is complete, an automated test exercising the guard exists in tests/scripts/ and passes in CI
  ← Satisfies: SC8 verification mechanism reproducibility (CI-runnable, not in-session-only).

## Considerations

- [Testing] Test must dispatch via the Agent tool with a realistic prompt that would otherwise invoke the skill — not merely grep for the guard string in SKILL.md (false-positive risk: guard text exists but never fires).
- [Reliability] The literal error string is the contract — any change to the string is a behavioral change that downstream consumers may depend on. Treat the string as a versioned contract.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a contributor, the SUB-AGENT-GUARD on /dso:onboarding is enforced and exercised by an automated test that runs in CI
